Subject: Inference deployment decision criteria — hosted vs dedicated (post-call recap)

Hi Samira / Alan,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the three primary workloads you mentioned (document search, customer chat, and batch reranking). Per our discussion, I captured the decision criteria that will drive whether NeuroScale should go Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, or a Private VPC/on-prem:

- Latency SLOs: customer chat needs p50 < 120ms, search can tolerate ~300ms.
- Throughput: peak spikes for chat ~80 concurrent users, baseline ~15 TPS; batch rerank jobs run nightly (5–10k queries).
- Data residency & controls: currently must keep logs for 2 yrs and restrict model debug data — potential VPC requirement.
- Cost sensitivity: preference for predictable monthly spend vs pure unit cost.
- Ops bandwidth: smaller infra team prefers Redwood-managed where possible.

Next asks we agreed on:
1) Can you send the traffic/profile CSV (TPS by hour, median & 95th token lengths) — I included a short sample template attached for convenience.
2) Confirm whether VPC-only deployment is a hard requirement for launch.
3) Any minimum SLA or uptime thresholds beyond standard (e.g., 99.95% vs 99.9%).

Quick guidance on sizing direction (high-level):
- If the priority is fast time-to-market and you can tolerate slightly variable unit costs, start on Hosted API and migrate to Dedicated once steady-state TPS is observed.
- If predictable throughput and isolation are important (sounds likely), Dedicated is a better fit; we’ll size the reserved pool by TPS + concurrency + avg token length.

I attached our Redwood Dedicated pricing deck and a blank traffic template to make the sizing workshop efficient. Proposed next step: 60-minute sizing workshop this week to walk the traffic profile and map to GPU options (A100 vs H100) and concurrency patterns. Are you available Thu 6/3 or Fri 6/4?

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Laura into the sizing session once we lock a time.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer

Hi Samira — thanks for the profile, I pulled out a few quick observations and a recommended starting point so the workshop can be productive: 

Summary observations (from the CSV):
- Peak chat TPS ~48 in a 10-min window, sustained peaks ~20–30 TPS for ~30 mins.
- Median token length chat ~420 tokens, 95th ~1,100 tokens.
- Search median tokens ~64, relatively low latency sensitivity.

High-level GPU guidance (short):
- H100 gives ~35–45% better throughput for long-context autoregressive workloads vs A100 (depending on kernel stack and quantization). For your 95th token lengths (~1,100), H100 reduces the number of GPUs required for the same TPS.
- A100 is still a cost-effective choice for mixed workloads and if you can accept slightly more nodes; good for early PoC to control spend.

Sizing quick estimate (rough, pre-workshop):
- Chat workload (peak 48 TPS, avg 420 tokens): ~2 x H100 (overprovisioned for headroom) OR ~5 x A100 (with batching/kv-cache benefits).
- If you want a single pool to serve chat+search, consider 3 x H100 or 8 x A100 to maintain headroom and burst capacity.
- For nightly batch rerank we recommend running on dedicated off-peak slots or a separate batch cluster to avoid impacting low-latency SLOs.

Concurrency & orchestration notes:
- Fewer larger GPUs (H100) reduces the number of hosts but increases per-host blast radius; can mitigate with automatic fallback and rolling deploys.
- Higher concurrency per GPU helps unit cost but raises tail latency for very long sequences; we usually shape concurrency based on sequence-length buckets (short vs long).

Dedicated vs VPC vs Private: 
- Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed subnets for audit and log routing; many enterprise customers run Dedicated behind a VPC with log forwarding to a customer SIEM. SOC2 artifacts and audit logs are available with our enterprise package — Laura can provide the compliance pack and templates.
- Private on-prem is only necessary when you need air-gapped or fully customer-controlled control plane; for your needs it sounds like Dedicated with VPC is sufficient.

Workshop proposal: Thu 6/3 10:30–11:30 PT — I’ll have Ben run through sizing worksheets and Laura will cover SLA/compliance items. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and the preliminary capacity worksheet (I’ll attach a filled sample).

Action items for workshop prep:
- Samira/Alan: confirm VPC requirement (yes/no) and any non-standard retention windows.
- Ben: prepare a pre-filled capacity worksheet with the numbers above for tuning in the call.
- Laura: prepare SOC2 evidence checklist and outline Dedicated vs Private differences we’ll need in the contract.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Karthik
